questions.stem: Name the two fundamental mineral ions plants require.
questions.modelAnswer: Nitrate and magnesium ions are the two fundamental requirements.

questions.stem: State what nitrate ions are needed to make.
questions.modelAnswer: Nitrate ions are needed for making amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

questions.stem: Explain why a magnesium-deficient plant photosynthesises poorly.
questions.modelAnswer: Because magnesium sits at the heart of every chlorophyll molecule; without it the plant cannot build enough pigment, captures less light energy, and the whole photosynthesis rate drops below its potential.

questions.stem: A gardener finds a plant with yellowing older leaves and stunted growth. Decide which ion to add and justify.
questions.modelAnswer: The symptoms point to nitrate shortage: without nitrate the plant cannot make amino acids and proteins, so growth stalls; adding a nitrate fertiliser restores protein synthesis and renewed growth, while magnesium shortage would show mainly as leaf yellowing from chlorophyll loss.
